question: When a conductor moves through a magnetic field, an induced current is produced. The direction of the induced current is determined by ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __Lenz’s Law****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lenz’s Law__ is a fundamental principle in electromagnetism.
 
• Lenz’s Law states that the direction of the induced current is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
 
• The law ensures the conservation of energy in electromagnetic systems.
 
• It is mathematically represented as E = -dΦ/dt, where E is the induced electromotive force and Φ is the magnetic flux.
 
• This principle is crucial in understanding the working of electrical generators, transformers, and inductors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Faraday’s Law:**
 
 
• It quantifies the process of electromagnetic induction.
 
• It states that the induced electromotive force in a closed circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb’s Law:**
 
 
• It describes the electrostatic force between two charged particles.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **Ampere’s Law:**
 
 
• It relates the integrated magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through the loop.
 
• It is a fundamental law in electromagnetism, used to calculate magnetic fields in symmetrical arrangements.
